column1: # THE SIX LORENAS OF THE 1869 ROSARIO CENSUS - IMAGE READ, 13 September 2026.
# Argentina, National Census 1869. Image ark 3:1:S3HT-XK5Q-L, DeepZoom level 13 (20 x 9 tiles).
# All six share ONE image ark, so they are one household on one schedule - not scattered.
# WHY THIS MATTERED: this archive's register groups LORENA with LERENA and LLERENA as spellings of
# one name, because the clerks disagreed. Guillermo (b.1853) and Geronima (b.1854) were flagged as
# "right age to be a parent of a child born 1882" - in ROSARIO, which is the whole question.
# The note on the 1869 census predicted exactly what the schedule would settle: household structure,
# and whether the clerk wrote Lorena, Lerena or Llerena.

column1: # *** THE VERDICT. *** The surname on the page is LORENA, with an O and a single L. The head is
# Peruvian, from Lima, a tinsmith; the five children are Argentine, born in CORDOBA. There is no
# wife on the schedule though he is recorded married.
# Pablo Armando's people were URUGUAYAN - the one Lerena baptised at Rosario before 1879, in 1866,
# has parents "naturales del E. Oriental", read from the act. This household has nothing Uruguayan
# about it and does not spell the name the way his family did.
# It is NOT a mathematical exclusion: Guillermo could in principle have fathered a child at Rosario
# in 1882. But the only reason these six were of interest was the possibility that LORENA was how a
# Rosario clerk heard LERENA. The schedule says otherwise - a different vowel, a different country,
# a different province of origin. *** They are recorded as looked at and set down, not as a lead. ***
# One echo worth keeping: FamilySearch full text showed an entire LERENA population at AREQUIPA, PERU
# that this archive had never met. A Lorena from Lima is consistent with that Peruvian population and
# with nothing in this family.
